title: UI libraries
description: Explore Algolia's UI libraries for building fast and engaging search and discovery interfaces.
abstract: InstantSearch is an open source UI library that lets you build search interfaces in your app using c...
abstract_enriched: InstantSearch is an open source UI library that lets you build search interfaces in your app using customizable widgets that you can combine to create unique experiences. Algolia for Flutter is an open source library that helps you add search and discovery features to your Flutter apps. Autocomplete is an open source, production-ready JavaScript library for building autocomplete experiences.
keyhighlights_enriched: InstantSearch Android
InstantSearch iOS
InstantSearch.js
React InstantSearch
Vue InstantSearch
The Algolia Flutter Helper focuses on business logic and helper components that you can combine into a custom search interface.
It works seamlessly with Algolia, but can also be used with other data sources.

title: Get started with the Algolia CLI
description: Manage your Algolia resources directly from the command line.
abstract: The Algolia CLI lets you work with Algolia’s APIs from your terminal. It’s great for interactive com...
abstract_enriched: The Algolia CLI lets you work with Algolia's APIs from your terminal. It's great for interactive commands, scripts, and continuous integration workflows.
keyhighlights_enriched: The CLI runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows, on both AMD64 and ARM64 platforms.
If you're running the CLI in an environment without a browser, such as an SSH session or container, run algolia auth login --no-browser.
algolia application select creates a local profile and an API key for the application if needed, so you don't have to pass --application-id or --api-key with every command.
If you're running the CLI in a CI pipeline or script, or if you prefer to manage credentials yourself, use the --application-id and --api-key options or environment variables instead of signing in.

title: Usage examples for the Algolia CLI
description: Examples for completing various tasks with the Algolia CLI.
abstract: The examples on this page use the application you selected with algolia application select. Where tw...
abstract_enriched: The Algolia CLI works well with other command-line tools, such as jq for working with JSON data. To create a backup of your index (records, rules, settings, and synonyms), use the following commands:
keyhighlights_enriched: algolia objects browse INDEX > records.ndjson
algolia settings get INDEX > settings.json
algolia objects import INDEX --file records.ndjson
The --attributesToRetrieve option only includes the name attribute in the API response.
You can combine this with the algolia objects delete command to delete all records with a missing attribute.
